verdicts.evidence: IDENTICAL on every leg: SELF identical; VERIFY identical; FREEZE identical; DRIFT identical. Close-up: no document read differently. The battery is sensitive to this function (it observed other mutants of it on VERIFY, FREEZE or DRIFT), so the null reading is a measurement. Measured 2026-11-04 on main a3a614f: dist/lib/tool-adapters.js sha256 1f610230f1c8bc2b…, the source embedded in the merged report of mutation-ratchet.yml run 41823718571, where this mutant survived pass 1 (the unit suite). Applied by splicing the mutant into the built file at the report's offsets, read back before measuring, pristine restored after; every node child capped at --max-old-space-size=256 and 20 s (a hang is a kill at 20 s). runward's own output read on four legs: SELF = `check --strict --json` on this repository (the self-gate, the reading of scripts/mutation-probe.mjs --function without --mission); VERIFY = `check --strict --json --path` on an `init --example` mission whose floor row hexa-architecture cites by file: pointers 39 crafted JUnit documents (40 with p20 for the mutants re-run in a second round) (and two by test: pointers), frozen by the pristine build: 21 parse whole and are sealed by projection (junit-projection-v1), 18 do not and are sealed by bytes (positive control: the pristine lock records exactly that split); FREEZE = `check --strict --freeze --json` on an unfrozen copy of the same mission, compared on exit, payload and the bytes of the lock written; DRIFT = `check --strict --json` on a second mission sealed, then rewritten (d1: a name sealed `a"b` rewritten `a&quot;b` beside a `x"y` that keeps the document non-legacy, which the pristine build names `changed only by the reporter's quote escaping`; d2: a case with no classname renamed, named `its JUnit cases or verdicts changed`). Close-up (attribution only, not the verdict): junitProjection, junitProjectionQuoteVariants and junitRootFailures of each document imported from the mutated build in a child process, 5 s bound. The same VERIFY and DRIFT missions were then replayed through scripts/mutation-probe.mjs --function <f> --mission <dir>, with the same observed classes.
verdicts.argument: On a self-closing <testcase …/>, the slice handed to xmlAttributes ends at `tagEnd + 1` instead of `tagEnd - 1`, so it gains exactly the two characters `/>` (tagEnd is the offset of that `>`). xmlAttributes matches `name\s*=\s*"…"|'…'`: a match needs an `=` followed by a quote, and the two added characters hold neither, so no attribute can be added; and no match that ended before them can change, because a regex match over the prefix is still a match over the longer string and the global scan proceeds left to right over the same prefix. A value cannot be extended either: the `"`/`'` that closes the last value lies before the `/`. So the attribute map, hence the name/classname comparison and the green/red reading, is identical for every input. Non-self-closing tags take the other branch of the ternary and are untouched.
verdicts.stableKey: tool-adaptersjunitTestCasesArithmeticOperatortagEnd + 1tagEnd - 1const attrs = xmlAttributes(content.slice(m.index + m[0].length, selfClosing ? tagEnd - 1 : tagEnd), legacyQuotes);
